transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Alex Martin (Orion Head of ML); Dana Ortiz (Orion CTO); Priya Singh (Orion Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
POC sync to review latest evals on candidate models, discuss pinning strategy for production pilot, fallback/rollback policies, and next steps around benchmarks and security docs. Team agreed to run a 1k-query benchmark on a dedicated pool and to test rollback/fallbacks. Some discussion about latency vs cost and differences between quantized variants.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, audio okay? 
[00:05] Alex Martin: yeah good here, thanks Jordan.
[00:18] Priya Nair: cool, we'll run through the results you sent last night and then talk model pinning and fallback plans, I have a few suggestions based on latency curves.
[00:35] Dana Ortiz: perfect, we're mainly worried about 95th p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens, and also data residency for EU customers, so we'll want VPC options.
[01:02] Priya Singh (Orion): yes, infra wants to understand the network egress and KMS flow, so any diagrams will help.
[01:20] Jordan Lee: noted. quick recap — we tested three catalog variants: rdx-large-v1 (float), rdx-large-v1-q4 (quantized), and rdx-medium-v2 which is cheaper but less accurate. results in the sheet show median latency on hosted low, dedicated middle, quantized had best cost but some drop in few-shot qa.
[01:45] Alex Martin: I saw that — rdx-large-v1-q4 did well on throughput but made a few hallucinations in the product-summary prompts, do we have samples?
[02:10] Priya Nair: yes, we flagged 12 borderline responses in the eval set, i'll paste examples in the doc after the call. Some of the hallucinations correlate with longer context windows, could be tokenization edge-cases.
[02:40] Jordan Lee: about pinning — our recommendation is to pin rdx-large-v1 as primary on dedicated pool for the pilot, with rdx-large-v1-q4 as fallback for burst/low-cost mode, and rdx-medium-v2 as cold fallback if dedicated capacity is exhausted, does that map to what you need?
[03:05] Dana Ortiz: that makes sense, we want predictable SLO so pinning to the float variant on dedicated is preferred. How painful is a rollback if we need to switch to fallback quickly?
[03:25] Priya Nair: rollback is fine — we have rollout policies: canary 10%, 50%, full. For immediate failover we support automatic region/pool fallback within the same model family; switching variants is typically <200ms for routing but warmup of KV cache can add 200–800ms on first hot path.
[03:50] Alex Martin: ping, what about cold cache penalties? our users care about tail latency for the first token in a session.
[04:10] Priya Nair: good point, cold starts show 300–900ms additional latency depending on seq length and KV size. we recommend prefix caching for frequent prompts and pre-warm scripts during traffic ramp.
[04:35] Jordan Lee: cost numbers — quantized rdx-large-v1-q4 cuts token cost by ~40% in our bench, but quality hit in rare cases; medium model is ~60% cheaper but lower accuracy on entity extraction.
[05:01] Priya Singh (Orion): infra question — if we do private deployment (VPC), any special considerations for KMS and audit logs?
[05:20] Priya Nair: for Private mode we support customer-managed KMS; logs are sent to your SIEM over secure syslog or S3, and we can attach per-request trace ids. We'll send network diagram and SOC2 pack.
[05:45] Dana Ortiz: also, can you map the model variants to the policy names so our ops can configure routes? we use terraform to manage infra.
[06:02] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll include model ids and recommended routing rules; we also have terraform snippets for policy attachments.
[06:25] Alex Martin: regarding benchmarks, what does Redwood need from us to run the 1k queries? sample traffic, expected concurrency?
[06:40] Priya Nair: ideally a CSV of ~1k representative prompts with labels for golden outputs, and a traffic profile (qps, concurrency distribution, seq length). We'll run them on dedicated pool with the three variants and upload raw logs and summary.
[07:05] Priya Singh (Orion): we can share the sample traffic by end of day; timeline ok.
[07:18] Jordan Lee: great. quick note on catalog differences — some model ids in our public catalog map to different kernel selections on different GPUs; the float vs quantized runtime path picks different attention kernels which explains latency delta.
[07:45] Dana Ortiz: competitor question: do you have examples where switching to Anthropic or OpenAI variants were better? we want to know tradeoffs.
[08:05] Priya Nair: in our tests Anthropic variants had stronger safety priors on dialog tasks, OpenAI's latest had lower latency on small-context queries due to optimized kernels, but neither matched our float variant cost/perf combination for long-context product summaries. we can add a short competitor appendix.
[08:33] Alex Martin: ok, good. about pinning — can we pin to a model version and then push a patch with small tokenizer updates without re-pinning?
[08:50] Priya Nair: tokenizer changes may change token alignment and could be risky; for small pre-tokenizer fixes we recommend a controlled canary. The console supports version labels so you can pin to model:rdx-large-v1@v2026-03-01 and then roll forward to v2026-03-10 via canary.
[09:15] Jordan Lee: next, fallback behaviour: if dedicated pool is saturated we can route to hosted fallback with throttling and an automatic degrade policy that switches to quantized variant after threshold.
[09:35] Dana Ortiz: does routing across regions affect PII residency? we need to ensure EU traffic stays in EU.
[09:50] Priya Nair: yes, routing policies can be region-aware; we can set strict region pins so fallback doesn't cross region. For any cross-region we can redact or route to private deployment.
[10:10] Jordan Lee: any blockers on your side to proceed with the benchmark and the pinning plan?
[10:20] Alex Martin: none, we just need the doc and the sample traffic. small ask — can you add a quick checklist for rollback runbooks?
[10:30] Priya Nair: yes, we'll include a runbook with steps, commands, and expected impact metrics.
[10:45] Jordan Lee: excellent, let's quickly recap action items.
[11:00] (crosstalk) Priya Singh: i'll upload traffic and SLOs by EOD.
[11:10] Jordan Lee: Jordan to share model ids + terraform snippet + SOC2/KMS notes by 2026-04-03.
[11:25] Priya Nair: Priya to run 1k-query bench and post results by 2026-04-02.
[11:40] Alex Martin: Alex to review bench and sign off or escalate to Dana by 2026-04-06.
[12:00] Dana Ortiz: thanks, appreciate the clear plan.
[12:10] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread, meeting adjourned.

End.
